violation_type.title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For (26 TAC §744.1205(a)(1))
violation_type.short_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on the information obtained in the DFPS investigation, caregivers were not aware of all children in their care. Caregivers were not aware of the child's absence until the parent arrived for pick-up.

finding_variants.text: Based on the information obtained in the DFPS investigation, caregivers were not aware of all children in their care. Caregivers were not aware of the child's absence until the parent arrived for pick-up.

Re-citing: One caregiver reported having 14 children in her group, after counting multiple time she had 13 in children in her care. The  second caregiver mentioned she had 17 children in care, after counting multiple times, the amount of children present in her group was 16. Neither caregiver stated the correct amount of children in there care.
It was determined that staff were unaware of which child was in care when during attendance the wrong child was signed in.
A caregiver was not able to identify a child who has special needs.

During this inspection a caregiver was unaware of the group responsible for. The caregiver stated fourteen children were present however ten were observed.  A caregiver responsible for a group of second graders was unaware of the number of children responsible for. The caregiver stated they were responsible for seven, however it was found the caregiver was responsible for an additional three children observed in a separate area.
During the inspection, caregivers provided inaccurate headcounts during two separate walk throughs of the operation. Inaccurate head counts were provided 6 times by caregivers.

Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: One caregiver reported having 18 children in her group, while a second caregiver mentioned she had 20 children. The third caregiver indicated that there were 15 children in her group. Initially, this totaled 53 children. However, after counting several times, I found that there were only 48 children present. The person in charge insisted there were 53 children, but the caregivers then recalled that some children had left for the day, which led to a revised total of 48 children.
Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: It was determined that staff were unaware of which child was in care when during attendance the wrong child was signed in.

Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, this standard was found to be deficient.  The Site Director was unaware of a child's name that they were responsible for.

Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Group Responsible For: Caregivers did not know the correct number of children they were responsible for during inspection. One caregiver stated there were 17 children with them when there were 19 children present. Another caregiver stated they had 8 children when they had 7 children present.
